Hong Kong Stocks Open Lower: Alibaba Falls Below HK$100 Mark as Five Major Tech Giants Retreat
sum: On November 12, major Hong Kong stock indices opened collectively lower. The Hang Seng Index opened at 24,121, down 194 points or 0.8%; the Hang Seng Tech Index stood at 3,995, down 32 points or 0.8%; and the China Enterprises Index was at 8,105, down 66 points or 0.81%. Leading tech stocks came under broad pressure, with Alibaba (09988.HK) opening 2.19% lower at HK$98.4 (approx. $13), falling below the HK$100 round-number threshold; NetEase (09999.HK) fell 2.03%, JD.com (09618.HK) dropped 1.89%, Tencent Holdings (00700.HK) slipped 1.37%, Baidu (09888.HK) fell more than 1%, and Meituan (03690.HK) declined 0.89%.

However, Hong Kong stocks did not halt their slide during the morning session—losses instead widened. The Hang Seng Index closed the morning at 24,092.89, down 223.03 points or 0.92%, touching an intraday low of 23,988.44 and briefly losing the 24,000 mark; the Hang Seng Tech Index closed the morning at 3,970.28, down 56.78 points or 1.41%; the China Enterprises Index stood at 8,086.20, down 85.25 points or 1.04%. Alibaba's decline widened from 2.19% at the open to 4.97%, closing the morning at HK$95.60 (approx. $12), with an intraday low of HK$95.35.
Note: Quotes reflect the November 12 morning trading session for Hong Kong stocks (closing at 12:00 noon).

In contrast to the tech stock trend, the semiconductor sector extended its strength. Hua Hong Semiconductor (01347.HK) rose 2.53%, Iluvatar CoreX (09903.HK) gained 3.46%, GigaDevice (03986.HK) added 1.44%, and SMIC (00981.HK) climbed 0.65%. Overnight, the US Nasdaq closed up 1.6% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index surged 5.66%, providing external support for Hong Kong chip stocks. By the morning close, Iluvatar CoreX's gain had widened to 11.00%, while Hua Hong Semiconductor and SMIC rose 2.66% and 1.51%, respectively; GigaDevice reversed from gains to losses, closing the half-day down 1.13%.

The nonferrous metals sector led the market's decline, with Northern Minerals falling more than 3%, Shandong Gold, Zhaojin Mining, and Lingbao Gold dropping more than 2%, and Zijin Mining (02899.HK) down 1.87%.

items.t: China's Second Round of Major State Bank Capital Raises Clears Key Hurdle: ICBC, Agricultural Bank CNY 260 Billion Private Placements Approved by Shanghai Stock Exchange
sum: A new round of capital replenishment for China's large state-owned commercial banks has made key progress. On the evening of November 11, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (601398.SS) and Agricultural Bank of China (601288.SS) separately announced that their applications to issue A-shares to specific targets had both passed review by the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

According to the announcements, the two banks received the Shanghai Stock Exchange's "Exchange Review Opinion on the Issuance of Shares to Specific Targets" that day. The exchange determined that their applications to issue shares to specific targets met issuance conditions, listing conditions and information disclosure requirements. However, the placement plans have not yet completed the full regulatory process. Both ICBC and Agricultural Bank said the matter still requires a decision from the China Securities Regulatory Commission agreeing to registration before implementation, and whether registration will ultimately be granted and the specific timing remain uncertain. They will continue to fulfill information disclosure obligations in accordance with regulations.

On September 6 this year, the two banks separately disclosed their placement plans. ICBC intends to raise no more than CNY 100 billion (approximately $15.0 billion) and Agricultural Bank no more than CNY 160 billion (approximately $24.0 billion), for a combined maximum of CNY 260 billion (approximately $39.1 billion), all to be used to replenish core Tier 1 capital after deducting issuance expenses. This is the second round of capital increases by major state-owned banks, following the capital replenishment completed in 2025 by Bank of China, China Construction Bank, Bank of Communications and Postal Savings Bank of China.

In 2025, the Ministry of Finance and other entities injected funds into four major state-owned banks through private placements totaling CNY 520 billion (approximately $78.1 billion) to replenish core Tier 1 capital. The specific arrangements were as follows:

Top 4% of Shanghai-listed companies generate 75% of net profit; tech sector's market-cap weight rises to 25% in a year
sum: The first three quarters of 2026 have drawn a sharp dividing line across the Shanghai Stock Exchange: companies with market values above 100 billion yuan each, which make up less than 4% of the total, carried three-quarters of the market's net profit. As of Nov. 6, the more than 2,300 companies listed in Shanghai had a combined market value exceeding 65 trillion yuan. Nearly 100 of them — the heavyweights with A-share market values above 100 billion yuan — were worth more than 34.8 trillion yuan combined. In the first three quarters, these leaders posted revenue of 18.6 trillion yuan and net profit of close to 3 trillion yuan, equal to 48% and 75% of the exchange's totals, respectively. Revenue and net profit grew 5.7% and 8.5% year-on-year, both outpacing the exchange-wide 3.8% and 6.0%, with profit growth ahead by 2.5 percentage points.

On earnings coverage, more than 80% of the top companies posted year-on-year revenue gains, and nearly 70% increased both revenue and net profit. The picture that emerges: the stability of Shanghai-listed earnings is increasingly supplied by a small group of large-cap companies, and the "ballast" role of blue chips is shifting from sheer scale toward earnings quality and supply-chain support.
Banks and energy anchor the market; electronics net profit up more than fivefold

By sector, banks remain the largest segment by market-cap weight among Shanghai's top companies. As of Nov. 6, the top banks had a combined A-share market value of 10.6 trillion yuan, and state-owned giants including Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (601398.SS), China Construction Bank (601939.SS), Agricultural Bank of China (601288.SS) and Bank of China (601988.SS) all posted steady revenue growth in the first three quarters. Energy, resources and traditional industries also showed strong earnings resilience: net profit at leading nonferrous metals, transportation and oil and petrochemical companies rose 59%, 28% and 27% year-on-year, respectively.

Electronics stood out for its elasticity. Including the STAR Market, 16 electronics companies reported combined net profit of 212 billion yuan (approximately $31.8 billion) in the first three quarters, an increase of more than fivefold year-on-year; even excluding CXMT, growth still exceeded 121%.

Visa’s Hidden Power: Earning From Payments Without Making the Consumer Loan
sum: Visa coordinates banks and merchants rather than lending to cardholders. Its history, incentives, financial results and competitive pressures reveal the economics behind the familiar card logo.

When a customer pays with a Visa card, several businesses participate in the transaction. The bank that issued the card, the merchant’s financial partners and the network perform different jobs. Visa’s position in that chain has produced one of the world’s most valuable companies, even though it does not operate like the consumer lender many people imagine when they see its name on a card.

Its equity value was approximately $789.82 billion in the November 5, 2026 snapshot. The attraction is a business that can participate in enormous payment volumes without financing each consumer purchase itself. The challenge is preserving the usefulness and economics of that network as regulators, banks, merchants and competing technologies seek a larger role in how money moves.

Visa’s origins lie in Bank of America’s 1958 launch of BankAmericard. The organization became independent of that bank in 1970 and adopted the Visa name in 1976. The transition is important: a payment system could grow beyond the customer base and geographic reach of one issuer by enabling different financial institutions to participate under a shared framework.

Regional businesses were combined into Visa Inc. in 2007, followed by the company’s public listing in 2008. Visa Europe remained separate until its acquisition closed in June 2016. These changes helped create the present corporate structure, but the underlying commercial proposition remained coordination. A payment network becomes more useful when consumers can pay in more places and merchants can reach more cardholders.

That relationship creates a network effect, but it does not make customers passive. Banks can work with competing networks, merchants can question acceptance costs and governments can promote domestic alternatives. The company must maintain incentives for multiple participants whose interests do not always align. A system valuable to a shopper must also remain commercially acceptable to the institutions and businesses supporting the purchase.

Costco’s Real Power Is the Bargain Its Members Keep Renewing
sum: Membership, a limited assortment and fast-moving inventory underpin the warehouse model. Its history and latest financial results explain the discipline behind growth and a demanding stock valuation.

Costco asks customers to pay before they become regular shoppers. That membership fee changes the relationship: people expect the savings from returning to justify the cost of belonging. The company's success depends on delivering enough value to renew that bargain year after year. Its warehouses, purchasing scale and limited assortment support an economic model built around frequent purchases and trust in the prices on offer.

The stock market valued Costco at approximately $472.19 billion on November 5, 2026. Behind that valuation is a retailer with large sales and a comparatively small net margin, rather than a high-margin software business. Understanding why investors attach such value to it requires looking at membership renewal, inventory movement, supplier terms and the discipline needed to expand without weakening the proposition that brings customers back.

The model's roots include Price Club, which opened in a converted aircraft hangar in San Diego in 1976. It initially served small businesses before expanding its membership approach. Costco's own first warehouse opened in Seattle in 1983. The two businesses developed around a similar idea: combine volume purchasing and efficient operations with low merchandise markups and a recurring membership relationship.

Their 1993 merger created PriceCostco, with 206 locations and approximately $16 billion in annual sales at the time. The Costco name returned in 1997. Those milestones explain why its history includes both the earlier Price Club experiment and the growth of the separate Costco chain. The resulting company carried the warehouse-club model into more markets while preserving the importance of the member relationship.

Kirkland Signature, its private-label brand, adds another layer to that proposition. Products sold under a shared name can strengthen loyalty when customers trust their quality and value. They also give the retailer a distinctive offer alongside national brands.

sum: China Construction Bank reported third quarter 2026 net interest income of CNY 160,888 million and net income of CNY 104,662 million, with nine month earnings also above the prior year and basic EPS from continuing operations at CNY 0.38 for the quarter and CNY 1.03 for the period.

The bank paired this earnings update with a RMB 2.142b preferred dividend plan and the nomination of economist Cai Hongbin as an independent non executive director, which together highlight both capital distribution decisions and board level expertise on credit, regulation and long term policy trends.
Attention now turns to how China Construction Bank's net interest income profile might reshape the investment narrative that analysts previously outlined.

Spot opportunities across the wider bank sector by scanning our curated 212 resilient stocks with low risk scores, which reflects China Construction Bank's focus on earnings resilience and disciplined capital return.

To own China Construction Bank, you need to be comfortable with a large, system level lender that leans heavily on net interest income and policy priority sectors such as technology, green and inclusive finance. The latest quarterly figures show this interest engine still working, which matters for supporting dividends and absorbing credit swings.

The short term swing factor is whether margins and asset quality hold as loan books tilt toward these focus areas and cross border activity. Key risk sits with renewed pressure on loan yields or regulatory limits that squeeze NIM or fee pools. The recent updates do not radically change that equation.

The most relevant piece of recent news for that equation is the preferred share dividend plan on the RMB 60b domestic issuance. A fixed 3.57% coupon and RMB 2.142b payout signal how China Construction Bank continues to manage funding costs while servicing hybrid capital alongside common equity distributions.

China's PBOC cuts relending rate to 1%; Zhongji Innolight and a dozen other A-share companies announce buybacks, stake increases
sum: At midday on Nov. 6, a wave of announcements from listed companies swept across China's A-share market. Zhongji Innolight, Eoptolink Technology, TFC Communication, Dongshan Precision, Victory Giant Technology, Hengtong Optic-Electric, Dapu Micro, Robotech and several other companies disclosed buybacks, share purchases and business updates in quick succession, with most explicitly stating they would use the People's Bank of China's recently lowered-rate relending facility for stock buybacks and stake increases.

The direct policy trigger for this collective move came on Nov. 4. The People's Bank of China that day issued the "PBOC Notice on Stepping Up Implementation of the Relending Policy for Stock Buybacks and Stake Increases," cutting the rate on the relending facility for stock buybacks and stake increases (the "buyback and stake-increase relending") by 0.25 percentage point to 1%, effective that day. Robotech directly cited the document in its announcement, saying the policy "provides strong support for listed companies to safeguard corporate value through buybacks and other means."

In the optical communications sector, the three companies collectively known in the market as "Yi Zhong Tian" spoke up the same day. Zhongji Innolight said industry demand remains strong, orders from major customers already largely cover all of 2027, and some key customers have given clear demand guidance for 2028. It expects order demand for 800G and 1.6T products to keep growing rapidly, with demand for next-generation optical interconnect products such as NPO and XPO gradually emerging in the second half of next year, applicable to scale-out and scale-up scenarios. The company said it is actively preparing materials and capacity to be ready for a bigger ramp-up in 2027.

Eoptolink disclosed that, as of Nov. 5, it had repurchased nearly CNY 800 million (approximately $120.0 million) of shares through its dedicated securities account for share buybacks via centralized bidding. It said production and operations are normal and orderly, with ample orders in hand, and that order delivery and capacity expansion are proceeding in line with business demand. items.t: Chinese stock sell-off resumes as rescue tools face scepticism
China Stock ETFs Draw 472 Billion Yuan in Countercyclical Buying; Can Beijing's Policy Blitz Hold the A-Share Floor?
sum: On the afternoon of Nov. 3, China's A-share market drifted lower amid a mix of geopolitical tensions, the approaching U.S. midterm elections and an earnings vacuum, with hard-tech and dividend assets falling in tandem. Then the wind shifted near the close: several broad-based ETFs surged in volume in unison, the market's losses narrowed sharply, and the SSE 50 Index finished in the green. The Shanghai Composite and Shenzhen Component closed down 0.82% and 1.21%, respectively, while the ChiNext Index was still off 2.73% and the STAR 50 Index tumbled 3.81%. A total of 3,309 stocks across the market declined.

The force of capital positioning countercyclically through ETFs was the day's most striking signal. Six broad-based ETFs topped 10 billion yuan in turnover for the full session. The ChinaAMC SSE 50 ETF (510050) traded 12.9 billion yuan (approximately $1.9 billion), nearly four times its prior-session full-day volume of 2.6 billion yuan (approximately $389.6 million); the ChinaAMC STAR 50 ETF (588000) traded 22.5 billion yuan (approximately $3.4 billion), up from 16.7 billion yuan (approximately $2.5 billion) the day before; the E Fund ChiNext ETF (159915) traded 19.5 billion yuan (approximately $2.9 billion), versus 13.1 billion yuan (approximately $2.0 billion) previously; and the Huatai-PineBridge CSI 300 ETF (510300) traded 19 billion yuan (approximately $2.8 billion). The China Southern CSI 1000 ETF (512100) and China Southern CSI 500 ETF (510500) each also exceeded 10 billion yuan (approximately $1.5 billion).

Over a longer horizon, this buying support has persisted for more than three weeks. According to East Money Choice data, equity ETFs have maintained net inflows for 21 consecutive trading sessions since Sept. 28, the longest streak of daily net inflows on record, with cumulative net inflows reaching 472 billion yuan (approximately $70.7 billion). By comparison, during the sharp market correction in early 2024 (Jan. 16 to Feb. 19, 2024), equity ETFs logged 19 straight days of net inflows.
Note: Data sourced from East Money Choice; "—" indicates the source did not disclose the corresponding figure.
On the board, computing-power hardware names led the selloff.

sum: Investing.com-- China's major state-owned bank shares climbed on Monday after the lenders reported their fastest quarterly profit growth in several years, supported by stabilising interest margins, lower deposit costs and steady asset quality.

Hong Kong-listed shares of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (HK:1398), the world's largest lender by assets, rose as much as 3.6% by 02:35 GMT, after the company on Friday reported a 10% increase in third-quarter net profit.
Agricultural Bank of China (HK:1288) shares rose as much as 2% after reporting a profit growth of 10.8%.
Shanghai-listed China Construction Bank (HK:0939) added as much as 2.3% after it recorded a 9.8% profit increase.
Bank of Communications (HK:3328) posted 10.1% profit growth, while Bank of China (SS:601988) reported a more modest 6.4% rise.

The results reflect easing pressure on lenders' net interest margins as banks reprice higher-cost deposits and benefit from monetary support and mortgage interest subsidies. Gains from bond investments also supported earnings.
However, weak credit demand, a slowing economy and emerging risks in technology-sector lending remain challenges for the industry.

The Hang Seng Index declined 0.71%, while the Hang Seng TECH Index fell 1.03% and the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index slipped 0.30%. By midday, 660 stocks had gained, 1,489 declined and 1,129 remained unchanged.

Technology shares mostly moved lower. SenseTime-W fell 4.39%, Tencent dropped 1.41%, Baidu Group-SW declined 1.36% and Kuaishou-W lost 1.32%. Xiaomi Group-W fell 0.79%, Alibaba-W declined 0.61% and NetEase slipped 0.21%. Meituan-W was among the few gainers, rising 1.16%.

Gold-related shares saw sharp declines after spot gold briefly dropped below $4,400 following a more hawkish stance from the US Federal Reserve. Tongguan Gold plunged 10.96%, Chifeng Gold fell 9.45%, Lingbao Gold dropped 9.12% and China Gold International declined 8.19%. Zijin Mining lost 5.59%, while Shandong Gold gained 3.53%. Nonferrous metal stocks also weakened, with Luoyang Molybdenum down 6.67%, Jiangxi Copper falling 6.61% and China Hongqiao declining 3.91%.

Most major automobile stocks traded in the red. BYD fell 6.69%, Leapmotor declined 6.54% and Nio-SW dropped 3.24%. Geely Auto lost 2.93%, XPeng Group-W fell 2.14%, Great Wall Motor declined 1.76% and Li Auto-W dropped 1.71%.

Property developers also faced selling pressure. China Jinmao plunged 14.65%, Greentown China fell 12.84% and China Resources Land declined 7.72%. Longfor Group dropped 6.70%, China Overseas Development fell 6.44% and Sunac China lost 5.19%. Hong Kong retail stocks were similarly weak, with Luk Fook Group down 8.38%, Chow Sang Sang falling 7.24% and Chow Tai Fook declining 6.91%.

Domestic Chinese bank stocks moved higher across the board. Postal Savings Bank of China surged more than 7% following its earnings announcement, while Harbin Bank gained nearly 7%. Bank of Communications gained nearly 4%, with China Construction Bank and Bank of China Hong Kong both advancing more than 3%.
The gains came after major state-owned banks reported stronger interim results, with signs that pressure on net interest margins may be easing.

CTBC Bank (00998.HK) also set a new all-time high since its listing. Market participants attributed the move to the six major state-owned banks delivering better-than-expected interim results last Friday, which served as the primary catalyst for capital inflows into banking stocks.

The bank had previously reported a 5.1% year-over-year increase in first-half net profit attributable to shareholders and announced an 8.8% boost to its interim dividend, exceeding some investors' expectations on payout.

Postal Savings Bank of China (01658.HK) delivered an even stronger performance, with shares quoted at HK$5.21 (approximately $0.6646), surging 5.15% to rank among the top gainers in the sector. China Merchants Bank (03968.HK) and Bank of Communications (03328.HK) both rose more than 2%, while China Construction Bank (00939.HK), Agricultural Bank of China (01288.HK), and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (01398.HK) each advanced over 1%.

The A-share market reflected the same wave of optimism. Banking stocks bucked the downtrend in early trading, with China's Bank of China up more than 3%, CTBC Bank up nearly 2%, and Bank of Beijing, Qilu Bank, and Postal Savings Bank of China all gaining more than 3%.

Behind the rally was the concentrated release of 2026 interim results by China's six major state-owned banks on August 28. Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Agricultural Bank of China, Bank of China, China Construction Bank, Bank of Communications, and Postal Savings Bank of China all reported year-over-year growth in first-half net profit attributable to shareholders, dispelling earlier market concerns that persistently narrowing net interest margins would compress bank earnings.

China's July Surprise: 1-Month Fluke?
China's Biggest Banks Order Retail Gold Traders to Exit by July 24
sum: China's largest bank just told retail gold traders to get out, take delivery, or watch their margin positions close, all before July 24.

ICBC, the world's largest bank by assets, will halt retail precious metals trading tied to the Shanghai Gold Exchange after end-of-day settlement on July 24, 2026. Postal Savings Bank of China, Ping An Bank and China Guangfa Bank have made similar moves, according to the South China Morning Post and notices from the banks. Retail clients have three choices. Sell. Close the position. Or take physical delivery. That's it.

The timing isn't subtle. Gold in Shanghai fell below $4,000 an ounce in June after touching nearly $5,600 earlier this year, according to pricing cited by the South China Morning Post. Some banks, including Bank of China and China CITIC Bank, raised margin requirements as high as 140% this month. You put up more collateral than the position is worth. At that point, borrowing money to hold the trade has stopped making sense for anyone still in it.

ICBC's own June 24 notice was dry, but the message wasn't. The bank said it would stop handling personal bidding services for Shanghai Gold Exchange contracts including Au99.99, Au100g, Au99.95, PGC30g, Au(T+D), mAu(T+D), Ag(T+D), Au(T+N1) and Au(T+N2). After July 24 settlement, mobile banking, online banking and branch counter access will be closed at a time chosen by the bank. If you still have a position after that, your ability to close, sell or collect metal will be restricted.

China's banks have been here before. In April 2020, Bank of China's Crude Oil Treasure product blew up when oil futures went negative, leaving retail investors owing money on trades many believed couldn't fall below zero. Regulators moved against new Shanghai Gold Exchange retail accounts within months of that disaster, and the clampdown never really ended. By December 2025, ICBC and China Construction Bank were already closing dormant accounts and returning unused margin funds to customers. This latest move finishes a wind-down that started years ago.
Platinum surged 8% on August 4 and another 6% overnight on August 6, climbing to roughly $1,761 an ounce by August 12.

sum: The Hang Seng Index once surged 805 points to 24,302 points on Wednesday, led by tech heavyweights, bucking the broad sell-off across Asian markets over artificial intelligence concerns.
The benchmark Hang Seng Index rose 702 points, or 2.99 percent, to 24,199 points at market close, delivering a market turnover of HK$375.84 billion.

Alibaba (9988) surged 12.21 percent, leading the gain as the best-performing blue chip. It once rose as much as 13.8 percent intraday – its largest single-day gain since last September. Bloomberg reported that analysts attributed the rise to reports of China's plan to restrict overseas access to its top-tier AI, which would benefit Alibaba's AI business. Preliminary forecasts for Alibaba's fiscal 2027 first quarter earnings show solid e-commerce profits returning to growth.
Xiaomi (1810) gained 9.52 percent. The company's official Weibo account released a poster titled "SKYNOMAD" on Wednesday –a new name and its brand logo – sparking rumors of its next large-size SUV.

In other tech stocks, Kuaishou (1810) rose 8.7 percent, Lenovo (0992) rose 6.9 percent, Baidu (9888) increased 6.33 percent, NetEase (9999) rose 4.19 percent, Tencent (0700) rose 3.82 percent, and Meituan (3690) rose 3.25 percent.

It is worth noting that, in addition to the rebound in old-tech stocks, previously battered new-tech stocks also bounced back. Knowledge Atlas Technology (2513) experienced a lock-up expiration on Wednesday but received endorsements from multiple institutional investors, who remain optimistic and plan to hold the stock long term. The stock rose against expectations, surging 18 percent at midday. Also, Minimax (0100) rose 2.8 percent. Chip stock Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (0981) also gained, rising 3.2 percent.
Bank of China (3988), BOC Hong Kong (2388), and China Construction Bank (0939) rose 5.6 percent, 5.24 percent, and 5.75 percent, respectively. HSBC (0005) slid 0.91 percent.

US equity plunge and gold's worst week in decades | Market Navigator
sum: US equity markets declined for the fourth consecutive week as geopolitical uncertainty, persistent inflation data and fading artificial intelligence (AI) optimism converged. The S&P 500 fell 1.9%, breaching its 200-day moving average (MA) for the first time since May 2025. The Nasdaq 100 and Dow Jones declined 2.0% and 2.1% respectively. Investor anxiety remained elevated, with the Volatility Index (VIX) near 27 and the CNN Fear and Greed Index falling to 15.

The macro backdrop offered little comfort. US producer prices rose 0.7% month-on-month (MoM) in February — the steepest increase since July — adding to inflation concerns ahead of any full pass-through from conflict-related energy costs. Chair Powell acknowledged the Federal Reserve (Fed) faces a difficult balancing act between slowing growth and persistent price pressures, and did not rule out a return to rate hikes.

Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang projected cumulative revenue from Blackwell and Vera Rubin architectures to exceed US$1 trillion through 2027 at its GTC developer conference. He also confirmed that H200 chip sales to China have secured the necessary permits, with purchase orders in place and manufacturing restarting. However, positive sentiment was overshadowed by the indictment of Super Micro Computer's co-founder for allegedly smuggling US$2.5 billion worth of Nvidia-powered servers to China. Super Micro shares plunged 33% over the week, while Nvidia fell approximately 4%.

From a technical standpoint, the US Tech 100 shows little sign of recovery and continues to trade below key MAs. The 24,000 level is critical — a sustained breach would confirm a descending triangle pattern, pointing to further selling pressure towards 23,000. Any rebound is likely to encounter resistance near 24,600.

The Hang Seng Index (HSI) declined 0.7% over the week, outperforming major Western indices as global risk aversion intensified. The modest loss masked significant dispersion at the sector level. Materials was the worst-performing sector, dragged lower by plunging metal prices, while Industrials outperformed, led by the clean energy segment.

items.t: Development Bank of Kazakhstan on Strategic Priorities and Financing
sum: ASTANA – The Development Bank of Kazakhstan (DBK) is one of the country’s key institutions that finances large-scale projects in non-resource sectors. As DBK marks its 25th anniversary this year, Botagoz Abisheva, deputy chairwoman of the DBK’s management board, spoke to The Astana Times, explaining how that role is evolving, and the bank’s key priorities moving forward.
“DBK’s funding strategy is built around mobilizing long-term affordable funding to accelerate diversification of the economy,” said Abisheva, sitting in the bank’s office near the EXPO area.

“We actively engage international investors, development finance institutions, and ESG-focused funds to share the sustainability agenda of the bank. Every deal we structure is linked to projects that generate long-term social and economic impact, whether it’s renewable energy, industrial modernization, or infrastructure that supports private sector growth,” she explained.

In 2025, the Development Bank of Kazakhstan reported solid financial performance, with net profit reaching 117 billion tenge (US$231.3 million), a 3.5 trillion tenge (US$6.9 billion) loan portfolio and a 2.4 trillion tenge (US$4.7 billion) leasing portfolio, while the share of nonperforming loans stood at 0.4%, according to the bank’s data.

The bank has financed 77 projects totaling 2.3 trillion tenge (US$4.5 billion), including 41 investment projects and 36 export-oriented projects, reflecting its focus on long-term development and external market expansion.
Turning to areas that hold potential for the country’s economy, Abisheva highlighted renewable energy and green technologies among the first.

“Second, advanced manufacturing and processing industries, particularly in metallurgy, chemical, and engineering. Third, logistics and transport, as Kazakhstan strengthens its role as a Eurasian transit hub. And finally, the digital and creative economy, areas where young Kazakhstan entrepreneurs are increasingly competitive, regionally and globally,” she said.

Here’s why the HSBC share price is in a strong bull run
sum: HSBC share price continued its strong rally and is now sitting at its all-time high, with its market capitalization hitting $300 billion. It has become the sixth biggest bank in the world after JPMorgan, Bank of America, ICBC, Agriculture Bank of China, and China Construction Bank. This article explores whether the stock has more upside to go.
HSBC, a top European bank, has been in a strong uptrend in the past few years, moving from a low of 277p in 2021 to the current 1,277p.
This surge has mirrored the performance of other European banks like Société Générale, UniCredit, Lloyds Bank, and Commerzbank.
This rally happened because of the relatively higher interest rates, which boosted its net income margin and income.

Most importantly, the management has been implementing a turnaround strategy that has seen it exit some of its unprofitable markets with the goal of increasing its emphasis on the Asian market. As part of this growth, the company announced a major acquisition of Hang Seng Bank.
It has exited its French, Canada, the United States, Greece, South Africa, Argentina, Uruguay, and Sri Lanka.
Additionally, the company is expanding its business in other areas, including wealth management, where it is aiming to become a major competitor to other companies like UBS and Morgan Stanley.

items.t: China Spotlights ‘Revolving-Door’ Bribery Case in Financial Anti-Graft Campaign
sum: A former senior executive at China Construction Bank (CCB) has been handed a 14-year prison term in a bribery case that lays bare Beijing’s widening crackdown on “revolving-door” corruption between state lenders and private developers.

Huang Xi, 61, spent more than three decades at the state-run bank, where she eventually held senior roles in investment banking, asset management and institutional banking. She left around 2018 to join developer Tahoe Group Co. Ltd.

- Former CCB executive Huang Xi received a 14-year prison sentence for bribery linked to “revolving-door” corruption.
- Huang accepted over 45 million yuan from Tahoe Group and others after facilitating business favors, returning all illicit gains.
- Chinese courts highlighted the case as an example of hidden corruption between state banks and private developers.

- China Construction Bank (CCB) is a state-run bank that experienced a "revolving-door" corruption case involving its former senior executive, Huang Xi. She used her position at CCB to benefit a company controlled by Tahoe Group's founder, receiving bribes for her actions. This case highlights Beijing's efforts to combat corruption within state lenders and private developers.
